# recall-eval-v2

Evaluation set for the offline retrieval measurement script `scripts/measure/recall-metrics.mjs`.
The set is measurement material. The script prints metric JSON and compares nothing against fixed values.

## Files

One JSONL file per subset, read from this directory and from `private/`. A missing file counts as zero queries. Blank lines and lines starting with `//` are ignored.

| File | Content |
|-|-|
| `human_ko.jsonl` | Korean queries written by a person (target 150 or more), kept in `private/` |
| `identifier.jsonl` | Exact identifier queries (names, settings, ids) |
| `temporal_holdout.jsonl` | Queries whose answers were created after `referenceDate` |
| `paraphrase_blind.jsonl` | Paraphrases written without reading the source text |
| `hard_negative.jsonl` | Queries with confusable fragments listed as `distractors` |
| `synthetic.jsonl` | Machine-made queries, reported separately and left out of the overall figures |
| `example.jsonl` | Format example, every line marked `"example": true`, read only with `--examples` |

`example.jsonl` holds synthetic lines. Its fragment ids exist in no database. Real files must not contain `"example": true`.

## Line format

```json
{"id": "hk-001", "subset": "human_ko", "domain": "ops", "query": "...", "tags": ["particle"],
 "relevant": [{"id": "frag-...", "grade": 3}], "distractors": ["frag-..."]}
```

| Field | Rule |
|-|-|
| `id` | Required, unique across all files, characters `A-Za-z0-9._-` |
| `subset` | Required, equal to the file name stem |
| `query` | Required, up to 500 characters, no two lines with the same text in one workspace |
| `keywords` | Optional, up to 20 strings sent as the recall `keywords` next to the query text. Without it the script derives keywords from the query (see `--query-keywords`) |
| `tags` | Optional, from `spacing`, `particle`, `en_identifier`, `mixed_ko_en` |
| `domain` | Required for `human_ko`: `research`, `coding`, `ops`, `schedule`. A `human_ko` query contains Hangul |
| `relevant` | Answer fragments of the target database: `id` and `grade` (1 related, 2 useful, 3 direct answer). Missing or empty means unlabeled |
| `distractors` | Optional fragment ids that must not outrank the answer. Not part of `relevant` |
| `workspace` | Optional. Without it the query runs over all workspaces with master scope |
| `referenceDate` | Required for `temporal_holdout` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), forbidden elsewhere. Answers are expected to be created after the end of that day (UTC) |
| `author` | Optional free text |
| `example` | Only in `example.jsonl` |

Unknown fields are rejected. `en_identifier` needs a Latin letter in the query. `mixed_ko_en` needs Hangul and a Latin letter.

Tags stratify the figures: `spacing` (spacing variants), `particle` (particle or ending variants), `en_identifier` (English identifier in the query), `mixed_ko_en` (Korean and English mixed).

## Real queries stay out of the repository

Real queries and their labels live in `tests/fixtures/recall-eval-v2/private/`, using the same file names (`private/human_ko.jsonl`, `private/identifier.jsonl`, and so on). The pattern `tests/fixtures/recall-eval-v2/private/*.jsonl` is ignored by git, and the script reads both the directory and its `private` subdirectory. Files placed next to this README are tracked: keep only `example.jsonl` there. Ids must stay unique across both locations.

## Adding human-written queries

Queries are written by a person who has not seen the stored fragments (a maintainer or a designated writer), in their own wording, and not generated by a model.

1. Write queries without looking at stored fragments. Cover research, coding, operations and schedule memories, with varied spacing, particles, English identifiers and Korean-English mixtures. Append them to `private/human_ko.jsonl` without `relevant` (unlabeled lines are counted and left out of the metrics).
2. Label afterwards, as a separate step, and never with the system under test: do not use memento recall, the search tools or any ranking of this repository to find answers, because the labels would then favor what that retriever already returns. Browse the fragment list instead (a database listing ordered by topic or creation time) or use a different retriever such as plain SQL pattern matching. Add `relevant` with grades; several answers per query are allowed. Fragments judged confusable go to `distractors`.
3. `node scripts/measure/recall-metrics.mjs --target <host:port/database>` prints `coverage.human_ko` with the labeled count against the target of 150.
4. Run `node --test tests/unit/recall-eval-set.test.js` to check the structure of every file.

Fragment ids refer to the database the script runs against, which is a disposable restore of the data. Labels that point to fragments missing from that database are listed under `labels.stale_fragments` and left out of the metrics.

Files must not contain personal data or secrets. Keep fragment text out of the repository; ids and queries only.
